text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Palestinian negotiator Shaath says King Hussein supported "our presence in Washington summit and Egyptian President Mubarak by his absence."
- 500,000 dinars ($706,214) of soft loans to local wheat growers to encourage farmers to cultivate grains.
- Release of four Jordanian citizens arrested in Bosnia.
- Information Minister Muasher says no official contacts currently being conducted to convene an Arab summit.
- Supply Ministry says it rejected a small quantity of imported Indian wheat (2,500 tonnes) because it was soaked with sea water after it was exposed to a leakage on vessel.
- Information Minster Muasher says the coming phase will witness intensified Jordanian-Palestinian coordination.
- Aqaba Regional Authority allocates large plots of land for setting up private resorts as part of efforts to boost tourism along the Red Sea port's coast.
- Prime Minster Kabariti returns home after end of U.S. summit.
- Two hundred and twenty-one projects totalling 301 million dinars have so far this year gained from the new investment law's tax exemptions.

- Jordan warns against renegotiating peace accords already reached between Israelis and Palestinians. Emphasises that immediate focus be given to implementation of the accords and resumption of final status negotiations.
- Regent says Jerusalem "events of grave anxiety but also a chance to present the issue to the world."

- Sixty-six million dinars is the total 1996 fiscal year allocated budget of Amman Municipality, after including the new appointments. The municipality council meets on Tuesday to discuss and approve the budget.

- Minister of Administrative Reform Kamal Nasser says administrative reform will encompass the private sector and is based "on the public sector employing the criteria of productivity and competitiveness."
- Government says has no financial ability to meet pay demands of engineers working in the public sector after they hinted at work stoppage.
